results.title: Contral: The agent which teaches while you build. | Product Hunt
results.content:
The problem we kept hitting: AI agents write code faster than anyone can read it, they say "Done!" when they aren't, and you end up shipping code you can't explain.

What's new:

Bring your own agent. Use Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI or GitHub Copilot CLI inside Contral, on your own account. Pick the model and effort, approve commands inline, and see every changed file as a diff.

Contral checks the agent's work. After each turn it compares what changed with what you asked for: nothing changed, a missing function or file, a broken file, or placeholder code. Smaller and free models get a specific correction automatically.

One-click undo of a whole agent turn. [...] \- checks every turn. when the agent says "done!", contral compares what changed with what you asked for. it catches nothing changed, a missing function or file, a file that no longer parses, and placeholder code. smaller and free models get a specific correction automatically.

7mo ago

One month ago we launched Contral on Product Hunt and hit #1 Product of the Week. Here's what happened since.

500+ developers downloaded the beta. We didn't expect that number this early honestly. The feedback has been wild, some stuff we expected people to love (the teaching layer) and some stuff we didn't expect at all (Defense Mode became the most talked about feature by far, people genuinely love being quizzed on their own code which was surprising). [...] @igorblink honest answer: i don't have a measured error rate yet and i'm not going to make one up. it's a model, so it can be wrong. what we do to keep it grounded: it explains the actual diff, not a guess at the whole file, and it knows what you asked the agent, so it explains the change against your intent. defense mode questions are built from the real diff too. if you catch a card that's wrong, send it my way, those are the most useful bug reports we get

Having a second model check each turn, with a one click undo for the whole thing, takes a lot of the fear out of letting an agent run. Do most people keep the Learn mode on, or mostly use it early on?

results.content:
> Contral is an AI coding assistant that teaches while you build. In Build mode, a repo-aware agent writes code and explains each function, pattern and decision as it goes, and it can also explain edits made by other agents such as Cursor, GitHub Copilot and Claude Code. Learn mode is a structured curriculum inside a real editor, with courses in Java, plus Python, JavaScript, TypeScript and Go in beta. Defense mode asks developers to explain AI-written code back after each AI change, quizzes them on it and checks their answers. Contral runs as an extension for VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Antigravity, Kilo Code and VSCodium, and as the Contral desktop IDE, currently in public beta. Learn more at contral.ai.
